title: Claude Code Project Structure
blurb: Your setup — not the model — is why you get mediocre results. The canonical .claude/ directory layout, file by file.
body:
"Your Claude setup is why you keep getting mediocre results — not the model, not your prompts." The canonical project layout:

  • CLAUDE.md — loaded at session start; project overview, tech stack, commands, conventions & architecture.
  • CLAUDE.local.md — local overrides.
  • .mcp.json — MCP integration configs (GitHub, JIRA, Slack, DBs); shared across the team via git.
  • .claude/settings.json — permissions & tool access, model selection (+ settings.local.json overrides).
  • .claude/rules/ — modular files by topic: code-style.md, testing.md, api-conventions.md; can target specific files/paths.
  • .claude/commands/ — custom slash commands (review.md, fix-issue.md) for repeatable workflows; supports shell execution.
  • .claude/skills/ — auto-triggered by task context; e.g. deploy/SKILL.md. Loads only when needed.
  • .claude/agents/ — specialized sub-agents with roles (code-reviewer.md, security-auditor.md); isolated context windows.
  • .claude/hooks/ — event-driven scripts (validate-bash.sh); automate validation, linting, formatting; block unsafe operations.
